documents.title: Sample AI Syllabus Policy Statement
documents.stance_why: The statement says students "are to refrain from using AI tools in this course unless with the express permission of the instructor", so AI is banned unless the instructor permits it, and it then sets conditions for permitted use. That is restrict, not prohibit (exceptions exist) and not delegates (a default rule is set).
documents.summary: A model syllabus statement from the Center for Teaching and Learning. It treats AI-generated submissions as academic dishonesty unless the instructor approves. Where approved, students must disclose, cite prompt, tool, date and URL, verify output, and ask when unsure.

units.why: The statement opens by classifying AI-assisted submissions as "forms of academic dishonesty", which makes unauthorized AI use misconduct; P36 fits better than P01 because the wording is about dishonesty, not a course ban.

"students are to refrain from using AI tools in this course unless with the express permission of the instructor" bans AI by default with instructor-granted exceptions, so it is a default prohibition (P01); P06 is not chosen because it speaks of the course rule, not a silent syllabus.
units.anchor: students are to refrain from using AI tools in this course unless with the express

units.why: "unless with the express permission of the instructor" leaves approval of AI use to each instructor, so the decision is delegated per instructor (P04).
units.anchor: unless with the express permission of the instructor

units.why: Item 1 requires "transparency about the use of any AI tool by disclosing" it, so this is a disclosure rule (P24).
units.anchor: Provide transparency about the use of any AI tool by disclosing

units.why: Item 2 says AI is "a supplement to and not a replacement for one's own work", keeping the student as the author and problem-solver (P32); P29 is close but this stresses not replacing thinking and work.
units.anchor: Use such tools as a supplement to and not a replacement for one’s own work.

units.why: Item 3 requires the citation to include "the prompt or prompts", tool name, date and URL, which is the specific-details citation rule (P25).
units.anchor: including (a) the prompt or prompts provided to the tool, (b) the name

units.why: Item 4 asks students to be aware of "limitations including biases and errors by double-checking and verifying the accuracy", i.e. verify AI output (P31).
units.anchor: by double-checking and verifying the accuracy of any content generated by using this tool

units.why: Item 5 tells students to "Seek assistance from the course instructor when in doubt" about ethical AI use, which is ask-before-using (P10).
units.anchor: Seek assistance from the course instructor when in doubt about how to use AI
